newsitem.title: RUSSIA: Ex-Moscow air cargo rates steady, business recover.
newsitem.headline: Ex-Moscow air cargo rates steady, business recover.

text.p: Cargo operations from Russia's leading air cargo gateway -- Moscow's Sheremetyevo international airport -- have become more active in the last four weeks with the end of summer holidays, but prices are unchanged on month-ago levels, freight-forwarders said.
Peter Vins, Vinlund Air's president, told Reuters that the air cargo market has been very active during the last two weeks, but tariffs have not changed.
"Tariffs were stable. Forwarders do not want to lose clients by increasing them," Vins said.
He said the company had shipments of between four and seven tonnes of cargo a week. "It's a good volume," Vins added.

Lilia Sirbu, manager director of Icaros International Cargo Service, said clients were more active in September tha in the two previous months. "We have many new orders," she said, adding the market would be most active by the year end.
"Competition between freight-forwarders is sharp now. I do not beleive that tariffs will increase," Sirbu said, adding that clients often suggested tariffs and forwarders agreed with them.
Igor Mordvinov, Burlington Air Express Moscow senior sales manager, said tariffs were unchanged compared with mid-August.
"But we see the market as very active after the summer holiday slumber," he said.
Mordvinov said the market activity was expected to peak during the next three months.
"We see lower tariffs if this happens," he said.
Mordvinov also said his company had signed a few big contracts with clients. He declined to name the firms and volumes of future shipments.

But Grigory Portenko, sales manager of Logimix, Air France cargo agent, said his firm's orders had been steady in the summer. "We have a stable level of cargo operations irrespective of the summer holidays period," he said.
Chief cargo manager Vladimir Pavlov of Soby, a cargo agent for Aeroflot and Vnukovo Airlines, said his company had stable export shipments.
Meanwhile, Ilya Maslennikov, a sales manager of forwarder Eruslan, said sales volumes were sharply down at Sheremetyevo airport due to rigorous customs clearance rules.

"Customs tariffs are higher here than around the world," he said, adding that many companies try to avoid delivery of its cargoes through the airport's cargo terminals. "They prefer to use trucks to carry cargoes from Helsinki to Moscow or find other airports," he added.
Maslennikov said the market became very active in the last two weeks. "We have many orders for export, but absolutely no import deliveries. Our storage area in Sheremetyevo is empty now," he said.
Many forwarders see the development of transit deliveries to internal Russian destinations as very promising.
Vins said the majority of air cargo business was moving from Moscow to Russian provinces.
"Lufthansa saw this tendency an is developing its network of routes in central Russian regions, the Urals and Siberia," he said.

Vins said that his company had some big shipments to China and Hong Kong. "Shipments from Moscow to U.S. destinations were stable, he said. Export shipments had picked up in the last two weeks although Vinlund Air had more import deliveries earlier.

Mordvinov said his company planned shipments to Tunis and Cairo later this month. "Russian companies want to carry machinery to Egypt and equipment to recently opened joint ventures in Tunisia," he added.
Sirbu said shipments for Europe of excise stamps for cigarettes, which were produced in Europe for Russian firms were stable.
She also said flights from Amsterdam to Moscow with flowers had stable load factors. "We see growing flower deliveries from Columbia and Ecuador to Russia next few months," she said.

Chris Lewis, manager for Chapman Freeborn Russia, also said deliveries of flowers from South America were very active in recent weeks. "Delta and KrasAir carried many flowers," he said, adding that there was a big demand for deliveries of this cargo in Russia.
